san-quentin-xways.description: A 5 × 3 base grid is supplemented by enhancer positions, split symbols and xWays. The number of possible routes can increase sharply within a spin.
san-quentin-xways.feature: xWays reveals a stack of matching symbols, while split mechanics divide positions and increase the number of possible combinations.
san-quentin-xways.note: This is no longer a game to read as a single static grid. Think of it as a system in which position sizes and the number of routes change during the round.

fire-in-the-hole.description: The mine starts with three active rows and opens up to six. The number of ways grows with the grid, while xBomb starts further collapses and multipliers.
fire-in-the-hole.feature: Each new collapse can open another row, increasing the grid from 64 to 46 656 ways to form a combination.
fire-in-the-hole.note: Follow the state of the whole grid rather than an individual symbol: how many rows have opened, and which multiplier carries into the next collapse?

starlight-princess.description: Matching symbols anywhere on the grid combine with cascades and multipliers. Its structure is closely related to Gates of Olympus, with a different visual presentation.
starlight-princess.feature: After a winning combination, symbols disappear. Multipliers appearing in the same sequence are added together before being applied to the win.
starlight-princess.note: A useful direct comparison with Gates of Olympus: the same underlying logic shows particularly clearly how presentation changes the perception of a shared structure.

cards.title: Pay Anywhere: from 8 symbols
cards.text: Starlight Princess pays for 8–30 matching symbols anywhere on the grid. A winning combination triggers a tumble, so one spin can continue through further sequences.

cards.title: Multipliers 2x–500x
cards.text: Multiplier symbols can appear in both the base game and the bonus. Their values range from 2x to 500x and are added together at the end of a winning tumble sequence.

cards.title: 15 free spins
cards.text: Four or more Scatters trigger the bonus game with 15 free spins. The underlying Pay Anywhere and tumble rules remain, with additional multiplier accumulation.

cards.title: Overall bonus multiplier
cards.text: During Free Spins, a multiplier appearing in a winning tumble sequence is added to the accumulated overall multiplier and increases subsequent bonus-round wins.

sugar-rush.description: A 7 × 7 cluster grid, cascades and multiplier positions. Repeated wins in the same position gradually increase its value.
sugar-rush.feature: A cluster of five or more neighbouring symbols triggers a cascade. Winning positions are marked and can receive growing multipliers.
sugar-rush.note: Watch the history of individual positions as well as the clusters themselves: a location where wins have already occurred becomes significant.

cards.title: Clusters from 5 symbols
cards.text: Sugar Rush uses a 7 × 7 grid: a winning cluster consists of 5–15 or more matching neighbouring symbols. After a payout, the symbols disappear and the cascade continues.

cards.title: Marked positions
cards.text: After a winning cluster, its positions are marked. If a new winning combination passes through a marked position again during the same spin, a multiplier appears there.

cards.title: Multiplier up to 128x
cards.text: The first repeat win on a marked position gives 2x. Subsequent wins on that same position double its value up to 128x.

cards.title: 10–30 free spins
cards.text: Three, four, five, six or seven Scatters award 10, 12, 15, 20 or 30 Free Spins. In the bonus, marked positions and their multipliers persist between spins until the round ends.

fruit-party.description: A large fruit grid, cluster pays and tumble sequences. During the bonus, winning groups can receive random multipliers.
fruit-party.feature: After a cluster, symbols are removed and new ones drop from above. During free spins, individual winning blocks receive multipliers.
fruit-party.note: A straightforward example of clusters without a complex accumulation system. Read the symbol group first, then the additional multipliers.

cards.title: Clusters on a 7 × 7 grid
cards.text: The original Fruit Party uses cluster pays on a 7 × 7 grid. After a winning combination, new fruit symbols cascade into the empty positions.

cards.title: Golden Fruit — Scatter
cards.text: Golden Fruit acts as the Scatter. Three or more of these symbols trigger the Free Spins bonus mode.

cards.title: Random bonus multipliers
cards.text: During Free Spins, each winning block can randomly receive a 2x or 4x multiplier. A single cluster can therefore receive multipliers in several of its parts.

cards.title: Combined multipliers up to 256x
cards.text: If several blocks in one winning combination receive random multipliers, their effects can combine. The official release for the original Fruit Party states a limit of up to 256x the initial win.

legacy-of-dead.description: A conventional Egyptian-themed grid with ten paylines and an expanding symbol during free spins. The base game deliberately remains straightforward.
legacy-of-dead.feature: During the bonus round, a special symbol is selected at random. When enough appear, it can expand to cover an entire reel.
legacy-of-dead.note: Compare it with Book of Dead: their similar structures show how small changes to a bonus can affect the experience of a game.

cards.title: Tomb — Wild and Scatter
cards.text: The tomb symbol both substitutes for ordinary symbols as a Wild and acts as a Scatter. The same icon therefore affects ordinary paylines and the bonus trigger.

cards.title: Free Spins from three Scatters
cards.text: Three or more Tomb Scatters trigger free spins. During the bonus, Tomb can appear again and award further spins.

cards.title: Random special symbol
cards.text: A Special Expanding Symbol is selected at random on entering Free Spins. It becomes the central bonus mechanic, distinct from the ordinary Tomb Wild/Scatter role.

cards.title: Expanding across reels
cards.text: When it appears, the selected special symbol can expand to cover reels, creating further opportunities to form a payout. Assess it by its actual position and the current version's paytable.

fire-joker.description: A compact 3 × 3 slot with five paylines, a respin and a multiplier wheel. One of the most concise examples of the conventional structure.
fire-joker.feature: Matching stacks on two reels can stay fixed and award a respin of the third. A full screen of matching symbols triggers a multiplier.
fire-joker.note: Minimal visual noise makes Fire Joker a useful reference: the ordinary payline payout is particularly easy to distinguish from an additional feature.

cards.title: Compact 3 × 3 structure
cards.text: Fire Joker retains a conventional structure: three matching symbols on an active payline form an ordinary win. The small grid makes the additional features particularly easy to follow.

cards.title: Fire Joker — Wild
cards.text: The Joker itself acts as a Wild and can appear in any position on all three reels, substituting for other symbols when forming a winning combination.

cards.title: Respin of Fire
cards.text: If matching full stacks appear on two reels without a winning payline, those stacks stay fixed and the third reel receives one free respin.

cards.title: Wheel of Multipliers up to x10
cards.text: When the same symbol fills all nine positions, the multiplier wheel starts. In the original Fire Joker, it can increase the total win up to x10.

rise-of-olympus.description: A 5 × 5 grid slot with removal of winning groups, a shared meter and interventions by three gods. Read the round as a sequence of changes to the grid.
rise-of-olympus.feature: Winning groups clear the grid and charge the gods' features. Clearing the whole grid becomes a separate objective within the sequence.
rise-of-olympus.note: Unlike a payline slot, it is useful to follow the whole grid and the charge of the features, rather than one route from left to right.

cards.title: Round Multiplier within one spin
cards.text: In Rise of Olympus, the round multiplier accumulates within one paid spin. Distinguish it from persistent progress between separate spins.

cards.title: Hand of God
cards.text: Hand of God is linked to the god present on the grid. Each character changes the grid according to its own rules.

cards.title: Wrath of God through the meter
cards.text: Filling the charge meter triggers Wrath of God, in which Zeus, Poseidon and Hades combine to help clear the grid. The meter is a separate source of progress within the round.

cards.title: Choosing a god in Free Spins
cards.text: Before free spins, one god is selected to help on every non-winning spin. According to the official description of the original game, clearing the whole grid in this mode awards an x100-stake bonus.

fat-rabbit.description: Five reels, five rows and fifty paylines. During the bonus, the rabbit collects carrots, grows and changes the course of the round.
fat-rabbit.feature: Wild carrots contribute to the rabbit's counter. Filling the meter makes the character grow and can award free spins.
fat-rabbit.note: The base game uses paylines, while the main visual progression takes place in a separate meter. An example of a feature layered over a conventional grid.
fat-rabbit.metricsNote: Push Gaming publishes 3 844x as the Highest Observed Win. This is an observed result, rather than a confirmed fixed maximum-win cap.

retro-tapes.description: A wide 9 × 6 grid, Cluster Links, cascades and multiplier tapes. A winning group can grow through connecting special symbols.
retro-tapes.feature: Clusters of five or more tapes disappear. Wild tapes can connect groups and increase their multiplier after participating in a win.
retro-tapes.note: With 54 positions, the action can be difficult to follow. Start with the boundary of one cluster, then identify which Wilds actually connected the groups.
retro-tapes.metricsNote: The current Push Gaming game page publishes RTP 96.47% and Highest Observed Win 10 000x. A separate official Push Gaming article dated 04.04.2023 confirms an RTP range of 94.46%–96.47%, so Slotfolio retains both verified RTP configurations and does not treat the observed win as a fixed maximum-win cap.
